subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains the separation of development, staging, and production environments and how to read configuration files and environment variables.
key_points: Environments are separated to protect production data and services.
Secret values belong in environment variables, not in committed code.
Configuration priority order determines which setting takes effect.
misconceptions: It is safe to commit .env files to version control.
All environments can share the same configuration values.
If code works locally, it will work the same way after deployment.
check_questions: Why must .env files be added to .gitignore?
What should you check first when a deployment fails with a missing env var error?

fact_candidates: Purpose and differences of development, staging, and production environments
Configuration priority order (defaults < config file < .env < OS env < CLI args)
practical_judgment_candidates: Diagnosing a deployment failure caused by missing environment variables
Deciding appropriate log level for each environment
error_interpretation_candidates: Reading a 'missing environment variable' error after staging deployment
Identifying the cause of sensitive data appearing in production logs
scenario_candidates: API works locally but returns 500 on staging due to missing secret
Production logs exposing user data due to debug log level
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing .env files are automatically deployed with the code
Confusing .env file priority with OS environment variable priority
